objective: Gate calm-water total resistance coefficient CT, plus sinkage and trim, for the KRISO Container Ship at model scale against the Tokyo 2015 workshop's own tabulated experimental data at three Froude numbers on two mesh rungs, with the measurement definition pinned contractually before any solve in the manner F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md establishes
rationale: KCS is the strongest reference-data position of the four naval cases considered, and that is a measured finding rather than an assumption. The Tokyo 2015 workshop spreadsheet vary_Fr_2-1.xls was parsed this session: six Froude numbers from 0.108 to 0.282 carrying CT, sinkage at FP and AP, mean sinkage and trim, fully open with no registration wall, model scale 1:31.59, Lpp 7.2786 m, design Froude number 0.260, and the geometry IGES verified downloadable from the bare host. Nothing needs digitising and nothing needs OCR, which is not true of Wigley and not true of the propeller reference. The machinery is present and verified: the install ships DTCHull and DTCHullMoving as complete interFoam free-surface ship templates with snappyHexMesh setup, staged topoSet and refineMesh passes, a forces function object on the hull patch, and a rigidBodyMotion dynamicMeshDict with a composite Pz plus Ry joint, which is exactly the heave and pitch pair a sinkage-and-trim case needs. Against that, two honest counterweights. First, per docket B7, configured is not active: this lab has never run a ship case, so the cost estimate has no measured anchor and is graded against the outturn per the charter's factor-three rule. Second, the F7a ladder rule blocks rung (b) and (c) behind a dam-break gate that still fails at plus 11.0 percent, and this proposal does not attempt to talk its way past that block; it is filed so the cost and the data position are on the record when Katie rules on the scoping question F7_marine_free_surface.md R1 step 7 raised, namely whether a dry-bed contact-line failure should gate a wave-making case at all
gate: Declared before any mesh exists. Reference: the Tokyo 2015 vary_Fr_2-1.xls experimental CT, sinkage and trim, with the exact sheet, row and column recorded in the pre-registration and the file hashed. Stations: three Froude numbers spanning the tabulated range and including the design point 0.260, frozen before the first solve. Metric definition pinned in the pre-registration on the F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md pattern: the force-averaging window and its transient-rejection rule, the wetted-surface reference area and whether it is static or instantaneous, the sinkage and trim sign convention and the reference points they are measured at, and the dynamic-pressure reference. Tolerance stated as a relative band on max deviation over the three stations, anchored to the workshop's own reported inter-facility scatter rather than chosen by this lab. Three-valued verdict per docket B2: PASS if max deviation over the three stations is inside the declared band on both mesh rungs and the fine rung is not worse than the coarse; FAIL, reported as a result, if outside with a settled force history; NO VERDICT if the force history fails its declared settling test on either rung, which is the outcome F8 actually returned on the nearest comparable stack and is therefore a live possibility rather than a formality
cost_basis: estimate with an explicitly wide band and no measured anchor, because no ship case has ever run in this lab. Anchored to the shipped DTCHull tutorial's own dimensions read from its dictionaries: base blockMesh 42x19x168 = 134,064 cells before snapping, snappyHexMesh maxGlobalCells 2,000,000, decomposePar numberOfSubdomains 8, controlDict endTime 4000 with writeInterval 100. Priced as six solves, three Froude numbers on two mesh rungs, at roughly 400 to 900 core-min each, plus meshing. The gap map's W3 item proposes running the DTCHull tutorial as shipped precisely to replace this estimate with a measurement, and this figure should be re-priced against that outturn before any large authorisation. Graded against the measured cost afterwards per the charter's factor-three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes. A pass gives the lab its first ship-scale free-surface credential against open workshop data that naval engineers recognise on sight, and it establishes a measured cost basis for every subsequent hull. A fail with settled forces is a real finding about interFoam free-surface resistance at model scale and bounds what the marine line may claim. A no-verdict on settling is itself the most valuable of the three at this stage, because it would show that the settling problem F8 hit on simpleFoam plus MRF also afflicts the free-surface stack, which would redirect the whole marine line onto instrument work before any further hull is meshed
hard_criterion_note: New case with no existing family in this lab. The nearest relatives are F7a, which is 2-D dam break and fails its gate, and the DTCHull tutorial, which has never been run here. Hardness is therefore genuine and is the reason the proposal is staged and pre-registered rather than launched as one block
